lines.x: South African stocks recorded their biggest intraday gain in nearly seven months, with the FTSE/JSE All Share Index rising 3.7% amid surging gold prices and technology shares.
Petrol and diesel prices in South Africa are expected to decline due to temporary fuel levy cuts, though rising global oil costs will partially erode the relief.
The African Energy Chamber forecasts a 175% increase in LNG exports as energy buyers seek alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz.
The US government announced that South Africa will be removed from the duty-free benefits of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) starting next year.
